pretexts: deepfake videos impersonating politicians, celebrities, and news anchors
trusted person promoting fraudulent investment platforms
public figure promoting merchandise or applications
emerging_tactics: AI algorithms to manipulate audio and video
impersonation of public figures using deepfakes

kill_chain_signals.contact: deepfake videos circulate on social media platforms
kill_chain_signals.pretext: deepfake videos make it appear as though the trusted person is promoting fraudulent investment platforms, merchandise or applications
kill_chain_signals.payment: fraudsters use the name of legitimate companies to lend credibility to the fraud and convince victims to send money

red_flags: Assume that a video which includes a public figure promoting merchandise or investments is fake until you can prove otherwise
Videos that seem too good to be true or show public figures saying something out of character
Signs of video editing such as unnatural movements, mismatched audio, or inconsistent lighting and shadows
Fraudsters will use the name of legitimate companies to lend credibility to the fraud
Deepfakes often rely on sensational or provocative content to manipulate viewers
key_quote: Deepfake videos utilize sophisticated artificial intelligence algorithms to manipulate audio and video to make it appear as though the trusted person is promoting fraudulent investment platforms.
title: Bulletin: Fraud using Deepfakes
